Day-level matrices in ldata$df

Source: R/utils-functional.R
mg_daymat.Rd

meteogal2lfdata() stores the validation code of every day (qc_<variable>) and the date of every record (fecha) as n_curves x 365 matrices in columns of ldata$df, so they stay aligned with the curves when the object is subset. These methods print them as a one-line summary per curve and keep the class when rows are selected. Use unclass() (or as.matrix()) to obtain the plain matrix.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mg_daymat'
format(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mg_daymat'
x[...]

# S3 method for class 'mg_daymat'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mg_daymat'
as.matrix(x, ...)

Arguments

x

An object of class mg_daymat.

...

Indices ([) or ignored (format).

Value

format(): a character vector, one element per row; print(): x, invisibly; as.matrix(): the plain matrix; [: an mg_daymat when the result is a matrix, otherwise a plain vector.

Examples

d <- data.frame(fecha = as.Date(c("2024-01-01", "2024-01-02")),
                station_id = "10157", temp_mean = c(10, 11),
                qc_temp_mean = c(1L, 5L))
ld <- meteogal2lfdata(df = d, vars = "temp_mean")
ld$df$qc_temp_mean            # compact summary
#>     10157_2024 
#> 1:1 5:1 NA:363 
unclass(ld$df$qc_temp_mean)[, 1:3]
#>  1  2  3 
#>  1  5 NA
